paragraphs: The paper studies how to predict charge density accurately without making the computation too expensive. Within density functional theory, charge density is a central description of an atomic system from which chemical properties can be derived. This makes it a valuable prediction target, but the authors identify a tension in existing machine learning approaches: their accuracy or their ability to scale is insufficient.

Their proposed recipe combines three design choices. It represents density through spherical fields centered on both atoms and virtual locations. It gives those fields expressive, learnable basis functions, allowing the representation itself to adapt. Finally, it uses a high-capacity equivariant neural network. The contribution is the combination of representation, learnable basis, and network architecture as a route to accurate, efficient prediction.

The authors report state-of-the-art accuracy together with speeds more than an order of magnitude faster than existing methods. They also describe a practical way to adjust the balance between accuracy and efficiency: change the model size or the basis size. Thus, the approach offers both a strong reported operating point and flexibility for different computational budgets.
neurips-2024-a-recipe-for-charge-density.tldr: A combination of orbital representations, learnable basis functions, and an equivariant network improves charge-density accuracy and speed.

paragraphs: This paper examines the Robot Air Hockey Challenge as a test of whether learning-based robotics methods can work on physical machines. Air hockey brings together immediate control decisions and higher-level tactics. Its dynamic environment also moves beyond the assumption of nearly stationary motion used in some real-world benchmarks, making deployment a central part of the task.

Participants had to address differences between simulation and reality, low-level control, safety, real-time operation, and limited physical-world data. These requirements connect the benchmark to the practical conditions that can prevent a promising learning method from becoming a working robot. The competition was designed to expose these pressures while encouraging researchers to develop different solutions.

The competition results favored methods that combined learning with prior knowledge over methods relying entirely on data under challenging deployment conditions. An ablation study further investigated real-world factors that may be overlooked when developing learning-based systems. Successful physical deployment by the strongest agents provides evidence that this benchmark is workable, while establishing a foundation for subsequent competitions and research.
neurips-2024-a-retrospective-on-the-robo.tldr: Robot air hockey exposes practical deployment challenges and shows the value of combining learning with prior knowledge.

paragraphs: CHASE addresses action recognition from skeleton sequences involving several interacting entities. Models built for individual entities can struggle here because different entities' skeletons follow different distributions. These discrepancies interfere with training the recognition backbone. The paper tackles the input representation through a normalization procedure that adapts to each sample.

The method learns how to reposition a skeleton sequence by choosing a new coordinate origin inside its convex hull, the region enclosed by convex combinations of its skeleton points. A lightweight coefficient-learning component determines the combination appropriate to each sequence. This constraint gives the learned shift a geometrically bounded form. An additional objective compares distributions across pairs within a mini-batch and guides the network toward reducing discrepancies between entities.

Together, these components aim to give the downstream classifier less biased inputs for recognizing interactions and group activities. Experiments across six datasets consistently show improvements when CHASE is attached to backbones designed for single entities. The stated findings support adaptive normalization as a way to make those existing backbones more effective in multi-entity settings.
neurips-2024-chase-learning-convex-hull-.tldr: CHASE learns geometrically constrained shifts of skeleton sequences to improve multi-entity action recognition with existing backbones.

paragraphs: Density ratio estimation learns a data distribution by classifying real samples against samples from a reference distribution. An attractive property is direct likelihood evaluation: the model can assign a likelihood to an input. However, the paper describes a longstanding difficulty in extending this approach to complex, high-dimensional data such as images.

Classification diffusion models connect that classification approach to denoising diffusion. Their classifier predicts how much noise was added to a clean signal. The technical foundation is an analytical relationship between two optimal predictors: a denoiser minimizing mean squared error for white Gaussian noise, and a noise-level classifier minimizing cross-entropy. This connection supplies a basis for building a generative method around classification.

The authors report the first successful image generation beyond MNIST by a density-ratio-based technique. The model also evaluates an input's likelihood in one forward pass. Its reported state-of-the-art negative log likelihood is specifically among methods sharing that single-pass property. The contribution therefore combines a broader demonstrated generation capability with an efficient likelihood-evaluation mechanism.
neurips-2024-classification-diffusion-mo.tldr: Classification diffusion models use noise-level prediction to enable image generation and single-pass likelihood evaluation.

paragraphs: Knowledge graph embedding represents entities and relationships with vectors. Assigning separate vectors through a large lookup structure becomes costly as a graph grows. Anchor-based methods address this by using representative entities for propagation, but their effectiveness depends on which entities become anchors. This paper argues that primitive anchor selection leaves useful performance untapped.

RecPiece selects anchors through relational clustering. It first clusters features of factual triplets rather than clustering entities directly. The number of clusters is set to the number of relation types, using relationships as a guide to organizing facts. It then chooses representative triplets near cluster centers and maps those triplets to corresponding anchor entities. The procedure combines the representative role of cluster centers with the descriptive information carried by relations.

Across six datasets, the authors report better performance than earlier anchor-based embedding models while using comparable or fewer parameters. These findings support the importance of anchor quality within an efficient embedding strategy. The proposed improvement comes from choosing representatives more effectively, rather than requiring a larger parameter allocation to achieve the reported gains.
neurips-2024-clustering-then-propagation.tldr: RecPiece clusters factual triplets to select better knowledge-graph anchors, improving performance with comparable or fewer parameters.

paragraphs: The paper studies a running count of a stream of bits under differential privacy whose protection gradually weakens with age. An item observed d steps ago has a privacy-loss guarantee of epsilon times g(d), where g never decreases. The task is to release the accumulated count at every step while controlling the largest additive error.

Without privacy expiration, the stated best known error guarantee is O(log²(T)/epsilon), while the lower bound is Omega(log(T)/epsilon). The paper shows a different picture with gradual expiration. Its algorithm achieves O(log(T)/epsilon) error for a large class of expiration functions. It also proves that any algorithm with error C must satisfy a lower bound on C multiplied by g(2C).

The algorithm matches that lower bound even when g(2C) remains bounded by a constant. This identifies a setting where improved counting accuracy is compatible with limited privacy expiration over that interval. Empirically, the proposed method exhibits slowly increasing privacy loss and substantially smaller loss for older items than a natural baseline. The theoretical guarantees remain tied to the expiration functions considered.
neurips-2024-continual-counting-with-gra.tldr: Gradually expiring privacy enables sharper continual-counting guarantees, with matching bounds for the expiration settings studied.

paragraphs: CRAYM jointly optimizes camera poses and a neural scene representation from multiple images. The resulting feature volume supports both rendering new viewpoints and reconstructing three-dimensional geometry. Its central choice is to match camera rays across views, using the feature volume to give those rays information about scene geometry and appearance.

This representation lets the method combine consistency between rays with consistency in rendered images during optimization and training. The intended benefit is to impose physically meaningful constraints on both reconstruction and rendering. CRAYM concentrates its per-ray calculations and matching constraints on rays through image keypoints, improving the efficiency and accuracy of identifying scene correspondences. Features accumulated along rays also allow the method to reduce the influence of a coherence constraint when the associated ray match is erroneous.

The authors demonstrate the method on novel-view synthesis and geometry reconstruction using both dense and sparse sets of views. Their evaluation includes qualitative and quantitative comparisons with state-of-the-art alternatives. The stated contribution is a shared geometric and photometric basis for improving camera estimation and scene modeling together.
neurips-2024-craym-neural-field-optimiza.tldr: CRAYM matches camera rays carrying geometric and appearance information to jointly improve camera poses and neural scene reconstruction.

paragraphs: Deep Graph Mating asks whether pretrained graph neural networks can contribute their knowledge to a child model without retraining, fine-tuning, or annotated labels. The authors first examine direct parameter interpolation and interpolation preceded by alignment. Both approaches operate independently of graph topology and fail to deliver the expected results.

Their analysis identifies sensitivity to parameter misalignment and complications that depend on graph structure. The proposed Dual-Message Coordination and Calibration method addresses these through the messages exchanged within graph neural networks. Parent Message Coordination optimizes the permutations used to align parameters by coordinating aggregated messages. Child Message Calibration then adjusts message statistics in the combined model to mitigate the over-smoothing identified in the coordination stage.

Experiments cover node and graph property prediction, three-dimensional object recognition, and large-scale semantic parsing. Across these domains, the authors report training-free knowledge transfer with results comparable to pretrained models. The findings support message-aware coordination and calibration as a way to reuse graph models where straightforward parameter interpolation is inadequate.
neurips-2024-deep-graph-mating-b19d0eec5.tldr: Deep Graph Mating combines pretrained GNN knowledge through message-based alignment and calibration without retraining or labeled data.

paragraphs: The paper concerns graph generation when the generated outputs must satisfy downstream objectives. Drug design is one motivating application. Although methods for optimizing diffusion models have advanced, the authors find that applying such approaches directly to graphs leads to suboptimal performance. Their focus is therefore on adapting the optimization method to the graph setting.

Graph Diffusion Policy Optimization, or GDPO, uses reinforcement learning to optimize graph diffusion models for arbitrary objectives, including objectives that are not differentiable. Supporting such objectives matters because the desired evaluation criterion need not supply a gradient that a model can follow directly. The method centers on an eager policy gradient specifically developed for graph diffusion models through analysis of this setting.

Experiments report state-of-the-art performance across several graph-generation tasks with complex and varied objectives. These results support the proposed policy-gradient approach as an effective way to connect graph diffusion generation to downstream goals. The empirical claim concerns the tasks evaluated, while the broader methodological contribution is an optimization framework that accommodates objectives beyond differentiable training losses.
neurips-2024-graph-diffusion-policy-opti.tldr: GDPO uses a graph-specific reinforcement-learning update to optimize diffusion generators for objectives that can be non-differentiable.

paragraphs: GraphMETRO addresses the diversity of distribution changes found in graph data. Graphs can be complex and heterogeneous, so a shift encountered outside training may contain several different components. The paper develops a graph neural network architecture intended to represent that diversity and improve generalization under these complex changes.

Its mixture-of-experts design assigns different shift types to different expert models. Each expert produces a representation relative to a reference model, while a gating model identifies the shift components present. An additional training objective aligns representations across experts. This alignment is intended to support reliable optimization, giving the specialized models a shared representational basis while they address different shifts.

The authors report state-of-the-art results on four datasets in the GOOD benchmark, which includes natural, complex distribution shifts. Reported improvements are 67% on WebKB and 4.2% on Twitch. These findings provide empirical support for combining shift-specific experts with representation alignment. The approach treats the diversity of shifts as something the architecture can model explicitly, rather than leaving all adaptation to a single undifferentiated predictor.
neurips-2024-graphmetro-mitigating-compl.tldr: GraphMETRO aligns shift-specialized graph experts and uses a gating model to handle complex distribution changes.

paragraphs: HydraLoRA targets efficient adaptation of large language models to new tasks. Parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA reduce the amount of model adaptation required, but the authors describe a performance gap relative to full fine-tuning, especially with complex datasets and domains. Their goal is to improve the effectiveness of this efficient adaptation strategy.

The paper builds on experiments that identify two insights into LoRA's training and parameter inefficiency. These observations motivate an asymmetric LoRA framework called HydraLoRA. A stated feature of the design is that it does not require domain expertise. This makes the structural choice relevant to both adaptation quality and the amount of domain-specific guidance needed to use the method.

The authors report that HydraLoRA outperforms other parameter-efficient fine-tuning approaches in their experiments, including approaches that use domain knowledge during training and inference. The finding supports the proposed asymmetric structure as a useful improvement within parameter-efficient adaptation. The reported comparison establishes gains over other PEFT methods; the motivating gap to full fine-tuning is the problem being addressed.
neurips-2024-hydralora-an-asymmetric-lor.tldr: HydraLoRA introduces an asymmetric LoRA structure that improves reported PEFT performance without requiring domain expertise.

paragraphs: LIVE studies how to use demonstrations efficiently for visual question answering. In-context learning supplies examples as context so a model can perform a task. Adding more examples increases inference time, and performance can depend strongly on which examples are selected. Combining visual and linguistic content makes these issues more pronounced for large multimodal models.

Earlier work on language tasks compresses useful demonstration information into a single in-context vector that is inserted into a model. The paper argues that these non-learnable vectors do not adequately handle a complex multimodal task such as visual question answering. LIVE instead learns an in-context vector to distill essential task information from demonstrations, making the compressed representation itself something that can be optimized.

Experiments show significantly lower computational costs alongside improved visual-question-answering accuracy compared with traditional in-context learning and non-learnable vector approaches. The result supports learned compression of demonstration information as an effective alternative to repeatedly presenting extensive multimodal context. The stated benefit combines computational efficiency and accuracy within the evaluated VQA setting.
neurips-2024-live-learnable-in-context-v.tldr: LIVE learns a compact vector from demonstrations to improve visual question answering while reducing computational costs.

paragraphs: LoFiT adapts language models by learning small changes at selected locations inside their representations. It builds on work showing that adding vectors to attention-head outputs can encourage desired behaviors. The paper asks whether learning these changes at task-relevant locations can provide a more effective adaptation method than existing representation interventions.

The procedure first identifies attention heads important for the target task, then learns offset vectors to add to hidden representations at those heads. It selects a sparse subset, comprising 3%–10% of the heads, and uses limited training data. Localization is part of the method's effectiveness: the authors find that choosing heads for the target task can outperform using heads selected for a different task.

On truthfulness and reasoning tasks, LoFiT's learned vectors outperform representation-intervention vectors such as those from Inference-time Intervention. Across seven studied tasks, performance is comparable to parameter-efficient methods including LoRA while modifying 20–200 times fewer parameters. These findings support both learning the offsets and selecting where to apply them as useful ingredients in compact adaptation.
neurips-2024-lofit-localized-fine-tuning.tldr: LoFiT learns offsets at task-selected attention heads, matching other efficient fine-tuning methods with far fewer modified parameters.

paragraphs: Audio-visual question answering requires a system to answer questions using both sound and video. The paper identifies a robustness problem: models can learn dataset biases too strongly, while existing evaluation data may not reveal that weakness clearly. It addresses both the way robustness is measured and the architecture used to improve it.

The new MUSIC-AVQA-R dataset starts by rephrasing questions in the test portion of MUSIC-AVQA, creating a larger and more varied test space. It then introduces distribution shifts to support evaluation across rare questions, frequent questions, and questions overall. Alongside this dataset, the authors propose an architecture using a multifaceted cycle collaborative debiasing strategy to counter bias learning.

The architecture achieves reported state-of-the-art performance on MUSIC-AVQA-R, with a stated improvement of 9.32%. Ablation experiments on both datasets examine the strategy's components. Further experiments combine the strategy with several baselines to assess its plug-and-play capability. Evaluation also exposes limited robustness in existing multimodal question-answering methods, supporting the value of the revised test setting.
neurips-2024-look-listen-and-answer-over.tldr: A revised audio-visual QA dataset exposes robustness weaknesses, while a collaborative debiasing strategy improves reported performance.

paragraphs: Frugal Flows addresses a difficulty in studying causal effects: models can be too inflexible, and synthetic benchmarks can be too simple to reflect real data. The paper introduces a likelihood-based generative model using normalizing flows to learn complex data patterns while directly representing marginal causal quantities of interest.

Its fitting algorithm uses observational data together with a parametrically specified causal distribution. For synthetic data generation, the model aims to resemble the empirical dataset while exactly satisfying a user-chosen average treatment effect. This combines flexible modeling of the observed data with explicit control over the causal quantity that a downstream method is supposed to estimate.

The authors also describe exact parameterization of the degree of unobserved confounding, and report experiments using simulated and real-world datasets. They present Frugal Flows as, to their knowledge, the first generative model combining flexible representations with exact parameterization of such causal quantities. This capability makes the approach useful for validating causal methods against controlled targets while retaining richer data structure.
neurips-2024-marginal-causal-flows-for-v.tldr: Frugal Flows learns flexible data distributions while exactly specifying causal quantities such as a user-defined average treatment effect.

paragraphs: AssetGen turns text into textured three-dimensional meshes with controllable materials. Its output includes physically based rendering materials, allowing objects to be relit realistically. This addresses a problem with generated appearances that already contain baked-in shading: the visible lighting becomes entangled with the object's appearance.

The system first generates multiple object views with separate shaded and albedo channels. It reconstructs color, metalness, and roughness in three dimensions using a deferred shading loss. Shape is represented through a signed-distance function with direct shape supervision, and fused kernels improve memory efficiency. After extracting the mesh, a transformer refines the texture in UV space to sharpen detail.

For reconstruction from a few views, the authors report improvements of 17% in Chamfer Distance and 40% in LPIPS over the best concurrent work. They also report 72% human preference over leading industry competitors of comparable speed, including competitors supporting physically based materials. Together, these findings concern geometric quality, visual appearance, and preference for generated assets within the stated comparisons.
neurips-2024-meta-3d-assetgen-text-to-me.tldr: AssetGen creates detailed text-driven 3D meshes with physically based materials that support realistic relighting.

paragraphs: Online budgeted matching concerns decisions made as opportunities arrive under limited budgets, with applications including advertising and service matching. Many algorithms assume each bid is tiny relative to a budget. Methods allowing larger bids often rely on fractional last matching, which permits accepting part of a bid when the remaining budget cannot cover it.

This paper removes that fractional acceptance assumption to handle indivisible bids. It characterizes bid size using kappa, the largest bid-to-budget ratio. The authors prove that any deterministic online algorithm has a competitive ratio no greater than 1 minus kappa. This establishes a ceiling on worst-case performance guarantees as bids become larger relative to budgets.

The proposed MetaAd framework produces different algorithms with provable competitive ratios parameterized by kappa throughout the interval from zero to one. The authors describe these as the first known such guarantees for the general-bid problem without fractional last matching. They also extend the framework to the fractional setting and use its competitive analysis to design learning-augmented algorithms.
neurips-2024-online-budgeted-matching-wi.tldr: MetaAd provides competitive guarantees for online budgeted matching with general, indivisible bids.

paragraphs: Online Relational Inference aims to discover hidden interaction graphs in systems containing multiple agents whose relationships can change. A fixed offline training set may not capture those changes. ORI instead updates its model through backpropagation whenever a new data point arrives, allowing inference to adapt as observations stream in.

The interaction graph's adjacency matrix is itself a trainable parameter. A new adaptive learning-rate method, AdaRelation, adjusts its optimization using the decoder's historical sensitivity to graph changes. This connects the graph update process to how the predictive model responds to different relationships. A separate augmentation method, Trajectory Mirror, exposes the model to varied trajectory patterns to improve generalization.

Experiments on synthetic data and CMU MoCap human-motion data report substantial improvements in relational-inference accuracy and adaptability compared with existing methods. The framework is model-agnostic and can be integrated with different neural relational inference architectures. Its contribution is therefore both an online updating approach and supporting techniques for learning changing relationships from continually arriving trajectories.
neurips-2024-online-relational-inference.tldr: ORI learns evolving interaction graphs from streaming observations using adaptive graph updates and trajectory augmentation.

paragraphs: Neural algorithmic reasoning trains networks to perform algorithmic tasks, often by approximating the execution steps of a classical algorithm. The standard setup processes one problem instance at a time. This paper introduces an open-book alternative in which a network can consult all training instances while reasoning about a particular problem.

That access is available during both training and testing. The framework is evaluated on the CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark, containing 30 diverse tasks, where it produces a significant reported improvement in reasoning capability. The central change is to make training examples available as a resource during reasoning itself, expanding the information the network can use for an individual instance.

The authors also explore connections across tasks by allowing attention-based aggregation of training instances from other tasks. This extension builds on evidence that multitask training can benefit certain CLRS tasks. They show that the resulting attention mechanism offers insights into relationships among benchmark tasks and supports interpretable multitask training. The framework thus combines improved reported reasoning with a way to examine cross-task information use.
neurips-2024-open-book-neural-algorithmi.tldr: Open-book neural reasoning lets networks consult training examples during inference, improving CLRS performance and revealing cross-task relationships.

paragraphs: Learning-augmented online algorithms use predictions while making decisions as information arrives. A common goal balances consistency, meaning performance with perfect predictions, against robustness, meaning performance under adversarial predictions. This paper shows that an optimal tradeoff between those two endpoints can still be brittle: performance may deteriorate dramatically under even tiny prediction errors.

The authors introduce a framework in which a user-specified profile controls performance as prediction error changes. The profile enforces smoothness while preserving an adapted analytical treatment of consistency and robustness. This makes behavior between perfect and adversarial predictions part of the design criterion, addressing a weakness that endpoint guarantees alone can leave unresolved.

The framework is applied to one-way trading. For that problem, the authors also address the pessimism of existing Pareto-optimal algorithms, which are tailored to worst-case inputs. Their new Pareto-optimal algorithm benefits from deviations from the worst case. A further metric compares Pareto-optimal algorithms through a dominance relation, providing a way to distinguish algorithms that share an optimal endpoint tradeoff.
neurips-2024-overcoming-brittleness-in-p.tldr: User-specified performance profiles make learning-augmented algorithms less brittle to prediction error while retaining adapted consistency–robustness tradeoffs.

paragraphs: PrivAuditor investigates privacy leakage when pretrained language models are adapted using domain-specific data. Such adaptation can be important because a general model may perform poorly on specialized tasks, a problem often attributed to distribution shifts. When the adaptation data are sensitive, improving task performance also creates a need to assess what information the resulting model may expose.

The paper benchmarks privacy vulnerabilities across multiple dimensions: data modalities, contemporary privacy attacks, adaptation techniques, and model architectures. This breadth makes the evaluation relevant to different ways of building customized language-model applications. The study systematically examines these settings and identifies factors associated with privacy leakage.

The authors pair that investigation with an organized codebase and practical insights, aiming to provide a standardized auditing tool for practitioners. The contribution is an assessment framework for evaluating adapted models and the conditions influencing their leakage. Its intended value is to help deployment decisions rest on faithful privacy evaluations of the customized system, alongside the domain-specific capability that motivated adaptation.
neurips-2024-privauditor-benchmarking-da.tldr: PrivAuditor benchmarks privacy leakage across language-model adaptation settings to support systematic audits of customized models.

paragraphs: Zero-shot temporal action detection must identify an unseen action category and locate its time interval in an untrimmed video. The paper argues that methods relying on pre-extracted foreground proposals restrict how text and visual information can interact. It first introduces a cross-modal baseline using mutual cross-attention throughout detection, which already outperforms earlier approaches.

The authors then identify a remaining common-action bias: the baseline concentrates too much on shared sub-actions because it cannot sufficiently distinguish visual parts relevant to the text. Ti-FAD addresses this with text-infused attention and foreground-aware action modeling. These components are intended to emphasize text-related sub-actions and separate relevant action segments from background video.

Experiments report results of 41.2% on THUMOS14 and 32.0% on ActivityNet v1.3, with stated gains of 11.0% and 5.4%, respectively, over prior state-of-the-art methods. The findings support integrating language throughout detection and explicitly addressing the tendency to focus on common action components. The approach connects category recognition with selecting the relevant temporal evidence.
neurips-2024-text-infused-attention-and-.tldr: Ti-FAD uses text-guided attention and foreground modeling to improve localization and recognition of unseen video actions.

paragraphs: Learning-rate schedules often depend on knowing the final optimization step in advance. The paper describes a substantial performance gap between existing schedules that require this stopping point and those that do not. Its Schedule-Free approach removes the schedule itself, aiming to retain strong optimization performance without specifying when training will end.

The method follows from a new theory connecting learning-rate scheduling with iterate averaging, which combines optimization iterates. This theoretical connection underpins the proposed alternative to an explicit schedule. The approach also introduces no additional hyperparameters beyond those used by standard momentum optimizers, so removing the stopping-step requirement does not add a new set of tuning controls.

The authors report state-of-the-art performance relative to schedules across problems ranging from convex optimization to large-scale deep learning. Schedule-Free AdamW also served as the core algorithm of their winning entry in the MLCommons 2024 AlgoPerf Self-Tuning track. These findings support the practical usefulness of the approach across the studied settings, alongside its theoretical account of scheduling and averaging.
neurips-2024-the-road-less-scheduled-2d2.tldr: Schedule-Free optimization removes the need for a predetermined stopping step while reporting strong performance without extra momentum-optimizer hyperparameters.

paragraphs: UKnow provides a protocol for organizing visual and linguistic knowledge in a shared graph structure. It divides knowledge into five unit types: within an image, within text, across images, across texts, and between images and text. A construction pipeline helps turn data collections into multimodal knowledge graphs following this format.

The motivation is to make more of a dataset's relationships available than a collection of image–text pairs typically exposes. The authors use the protocol to build a dataset from public international news. It contains 1,388,568 nodes, including 571,791 vision-related nodes, and 3,673,817 triplets. Event annotations add 11 coarse labels and 9,185 fine labels, providing another level of organization within the collection.

Experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate the potential of this single dataset to support commonsense reasoning and improve vision-language pretraining. The stated benefit comes from its unified organization of knowledge. The work therefore contributes both a reusable data protocol and a large dataset illustrating how graph-based relationships can support multiple forms of multimodal learning.
neurips-2024-uknow-a-unified-knowledge-p.tldr: UKnow organizes visual and linguistic relationships into multimodal knowledge graphs that support reasoning and vision-language pretraining.

paragraphs: Deep equilibrium models are implicit neural networks known for memory efficiency and competitive performance, but their learned representations have received relatively limited theoretical analysis. This paper examines those representations through neural collapse, a phenomenon describing the geometry of class features and classifier weights during training. The analysis covers both balanced and imbalanced class settings.

The authors theoretically establish neural collapse in deep equilibrium models under balanced conditions. Under imbalance, minority collapse is still present, but the models exhibit advantages over explicit neural networks. These include convergence of extracted features toward the vertices of a simplex equiangular tight frame, a highly regular geometric arrangement, and self-duality properties under mild conditions.

Experiments in balanced and imbalanced scenarios validate the theoretical analyses. The findings extend a representation-analysis tool widely studied in explicit networks to implicit models. They also identify favorable geometric properties under class imbalance, while retaining the stated conditions and the presence of minority collapse. The advantage described is therefore grounded in the particular representation properties analyzed and experimentally examined.
neurips-2024-understanding-representatio.tldr: Neural-collapse analysis reveals structured representations in deep equilibrium models and conditional geometric advantages under class imbalance.
